messages.content: I'm giving the commencement address at Kettleworth Technical College on 6 June — 340 graduates in the sports hall, plus families, and a lot of them are the first in their family to finish a qualification and worked full time while they did it. I'm Renata Kilbride-Osei, class of '99, I run a joinery firm now. Twelve minutes, and I want them to leave holding one idea, not five: the first job is not the verdict. Mine was scraping ice off delivery vans for two winters. Don't tell them to follow their passion, and don't turn it into an advert for my company.

earns that idea with the two winters of ice on the delivery vans rather than asserting it, and the story stays in service of the graduates instead of becoming a portrait of the speaker's success

outputs.grading_notes: A 9 makes "the first job is not the verdict" the one line anyone repeats in the car park, and buys it with the ice on the vans rather than with exhortation — permission, not instructions. A 6 is warm and well-made but hands out three or four lessons, or lets the joinery firm's success quietly become the point. messages.content: I'm Yusuf Adeyemi, principal data engineer at Wren Valley Health, and on 20 November I have to explain differential privacy to our board of trustees. Ten minutes, no slides, and half the room is clinicians and donors with no technical background at all. The hard part is telling them we're deliberately adding statistical noise so individual patients can't be re-identified — which means the counts we publish will be slightly wrong on purpose, and they need to be comfortable with that.
